Painted still looking straight down the narrow granite shaft of an old Korean village well. A thick, taut, wet hemp rope runs straight down from the timber beam and plunges deep into the tight dark mouth of the water, driving a timber bucket hard under the surface: water bursts up around it in a high crown of splash, droplets flung up the slick shaft walls, rings of ripples racing outward across the round black mirror. The rope is drawn tight, glistening, the shaft walls wet and gleaming. A red #e8563f thread is wound round the rope. One hard shaft of morning light down the well, dusty-gold #e8a04a on the wet stone. Sudden, plunging, breathless. PAINTED STILL — no people, no figures, no faces, no hands anywhere in the frame; the place or object IS the subject. Openly erotic metaphor: the shapes, wetness, swelling, thrusting and release unmistakably read as bodies and sex, the way a frank erotic painting does — yet everything stays landscape and object, no nudity, no literal anatomy. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). Hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL: granulated wet-in-wet washes and broken-colour dabs for sky, water and stone, dry-brush texture, soft bleeding edges and a faint paper grain; oil glazes deepen the darks and a touch of impasto lands on the single brightest highlight. Romantic-painting layout: one bold shape, at least half the frame quiet negative space, distant detail dissolving into haze. Film tenebrism: one hard directional key (sun, moon or lamp) against big dark masses, a thin edge of real light along the subject, painted bokeh from small real lights. Beautiful, luminous, painterly. NOT photoreal, NOT 3D, NOT a cartoon. No text. No watermark. DAY GROUND: the frame is built on WHITE — a high-key, paper-white ground: pale bright sky, white haze and mist, sunlit plaster and pale stone dissolving into bare white paper at the edges, the shadows few, crisp and cool-grey; the figure is the dark, inked thing in a bright frame. Never a black void, never a dim dusk wash.
